sehemu: Part V: Court of Appeal of the United Republic
jina: Chief Justice and Justices of Appeal and their appointment
maudhui: (1) There shall be a Chief Justice of the Judiciary of Tanzania and not fewer than four other Justices of Appeal, provided that a special sitting of the full Court shall be duly constituted if it consists of not fewer than five Justices of Appeal. (2) The Chief Justice shall be appointed by the President from among persons qualified to be appointed a Justice of Appeal and shall be the head of the Court of Appeal and also head of the Judiciary of Tanzania as provided in Article 116, and shall hold office until attaining the retirement age of a Justice of Appeal unless he resigns, his office becomes vacant by reason of illness or death, or he is removed from the office of Chief Justice by the President. (3) The other Justices of Appeal shall be appointed by the President, after consultation with the Chief Justice, from among persons qualified for appointment as Judges of the High Court of the United Republic under Article 109 or persons qualified for appointment as Judges of the High Court of Zanzibar under the laws applicable in Zanzibar, who have possessed such qualifications for not less than fifteen years. (4) Where the office of Chief Justice is vacant, the Chief Justice is absent from Tanzania, or is unable to perform his functions for any reason, and the President considers it appropriate to appoint an Acting Chief Justice, the President may appoint an Acting Chief Justice from among the Justices of Appeal. (5) An Acting Chief Justice shall perform the functions of Chief Justice until another Chief Justice is appointed or until the substantive Chief Justice returns to office. (6) Where the office of a Justice of Appeal is vacant, a Justice of Appeal is appointed Acting Chief Justice, a Justice of Appeal is unable to perform his functions, or the Chief Justice advises the President that the work of the Court of Appeal requires an Acting Justice of Appeal, the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice, appoint an Acting Justice of Appeal from among persons qualified for appointment as Justices of Appeal. (7) A person appointed Acting Justice of Appeal shall continue in office for the period specified at appointment or, if no period is specified, until the appointment is revoked by the President; notwithstanding expiry or revocation, that person may continue to act until completing preparation and delivery of judgment. (8) For avoidance of doubt concerning subarticle (1) and Article 119, a person appointed Acting Justice of Appeal shall have the full authority and functions of a Justice of Appeal, and the number of Justices referred to in Article 122 shall not be affected. (9) The office of a Justice of Appeal shall not be abolished while there is a person holding that office.
vifungu: (1) There shall be a Chief Justice of the Judiciary of Tanzania and not fewer than four other Justices of Appeal, provided that a special sitting of the full Court shall be duly constituted if it consists of not fewer than five Justices of Appeal.

(2) The Chief Justice shall be appointed by the President from among persons qualified to be appointed a Justice of Appeal and shall be the head of the Court of Appeal and also head of the Judiciary of Tanzania as provided in Article 116, and shall hold office until attaining the retirement age of a Justice of Appeal unless he resigns, his office becomes vacant by reason of illness or death, or he is removed from the office of Chief Justice by the President.

(3) The other Justices of Appeal shall be appointed by the President, after consultation with the Chief Justice, from among persons qualified for appointment as Judges of the High Court of the United Republic under Article 109 or persons qualified for appointment as Judges of the High Court of Zanzibar under the laws applicable in Zanzibar, who have possessed such qualifications for not less than fifteen years.

(4) Where the office of Chief Justice is vacant, the Chief Justice is absent from Tanzania, or is unable to perform his functions for any reason, and the President considers it appropriate to appoint an Acting Chief Justice, the President may appoint an Acting Chief Justice from among the Justices of Appeal.
(5) An Acting Chief Justice shall perform the functions of Chief Justice until another Chief Justice is appointed or until the substantive Chief Justice returns to office.

(6) Where the office of a Justice of Appeal is vacant, a Justice of Appeal is appointed Acting Chief Justice, a Justice of Appeal is unable to perform his functions, or the Chief Justice advises the President that the work of the Court of Appeal requires an Acting Justice of Appeal, the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice, appoint an Acting Justice of Appeal from among persons qualified for appointment as Justices of Appeal.

(7) A person appointed Acting Justice of Appeal shall continue in office for the period specified at appointment or, if no period is specified, until the appointment is revoked by the President; notwithstanding expiry or revocation, that person may continue to act until completing preparation and delivery of judgment.

(8) For avoidance of doubt concerning subarticle (1) and Article 119, a person appointed Acting Justice of Appeal shall have the full authority and functions of a Justice of Appeal, and the number of Justices referred to in Article 122 shall not be affected.
(9) The office of a Justice of Appeal shall not be abolished while there is a person holding that office.
